paragraphs: He claimed that the Creator — exalted — created only one angel, and that this angel is the one who created the whole world, who sent the prophets, dispatched the messengers, established the miracles, and commanded and forbade; and he it is who originates whatever comes to be in the world — not the first Creator. He claimed that the levirate (yibbum) is obligatory only upon the king. He claimed that the saying of Scripture [Deut 21:15] "וְהָיָה הַבֵּן הַבְּכוֹר לַשְּׂנִיאָה" requires that the beloved [wife], even if she preceded in bearing, her son is not the firstborn; rather the firstborn is according to the unloved [wife], whether earlier or later — after both are firstborn. He claimed that the saying of Scripture [Exod 22:1] "אִם בַּמַּחְתֶּרֶת יִמָּצֵא הַגַּנָּב וְהֻכָּה וָמֵת" was meant for any breach whatever — even an old breach that he did not dig himself and [made] not by demolition. He claimed that the saying of Scripture [Deut 23:16] "לֹא תַסְגִּיר עֶבֶד אֶל אֲדֹנָיו" [means]: if he was the slave of one of the Children of Israel and fled from him to you, it is not permitted for you to return him to him. He forbade marriage to a nursing woman, and made the obligations binding upon a minor from the time he speaks.
§2 — The course of the month; slaughter; impurity

He used to permit the taking of the heads of the months by the [calculated] number — except Nisan and Tishrei: these he permitted to be taken only by the sighting of the new moon. He also held that the slaughter of a bird [requires] cutting (dhabḥ) and severing the neck (meliqah) together. He claimed that the consecrated [woman], if a man forced her in the wilderness even with her consent, is not obliged to be put to death. He claimed that one who came forth from the womb dead does not convey impurity from it; rather the impurity is from one who died in the open air. He claimed that the grave which conveys impurity to one who draws near it is the grave that is outside; but the grave that is within a house does not convey impurity to one who draws near it. He claimed that the garments of a woman with a flux, in which she lay and which had become for her a riding-seat or a sitting-place — if a man drew near them while they were stripped off her, he becomes impure from them and must wash his clothes; but if he drew near them while they were worn, he need only wash the body. He claimed that the time of the aṣīl does not receive impurity — that is, it is a time in which a person does not become impure.

: The famous doctrine of the "created angel" (cf. the Maghāriyya, bab 7 above): the anthropomorphic scriptural expressions, and the work of creation itself, are referred to a single created world-angel, not to the primordial God. See Wolfson, "The Pre-Existent Angel of the Magharians and al-Nahawendi," JQR 51 (1960–61).
: A distinctive view of Benjamin's: the obligations bind a minor from the time he can speak, not from the age of majority.
: The two modes of slaughtering a bird: meliqah (pinching the neck by the nail) and sheḥiṭah (cutting the windpipe and gullet by a blade); Benjamin requires both together — a distinctive combination.
